expertInsight: Salesforce now calls Pardot Marketing Cloud Account Engagement. The product name changed in 2022; the certification may still use the Pardot name. In study materials, look for both names.

whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Account Engagement Consultant exam for?

personas.label: B2B marketing automation consultants
personas.description: You plan and set up Account Engagement for B2B clients, and want to show that you can guide an implementation.

personas.label: Marketing operations managers
personas.description: You lead your company’s marketing operations and need to plan scoring, nurture programs, and Salesforce data sync.

personas.label: Salesforce consultants adding B2B marketing skills
personas.description: You already work with Salesforce and want to add B2B marketing solution design to your consulting skills.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Account Engagement Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Account Engagement Consultant exam tests how you design a B2B marketing solution for a client. Be ready to connect scoring, grading, nurture programs, Salesforce sync, and campaign reporting to the client’s goals. Hands-on implementation experience helps you judge which design fits.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
68% to pass, which is 41 correct answers out of 60.
Solution design: Questions may ask you to choose a scoring approach, build a nurture path, or plan Salesforce sync for a stated need.
Marketing and sales alignment: Know how prospect data, campaign tracking, user permissions, and reporting support both teams.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use Salesforce’s current exam guide as your checklist. For each topic, practice explaining why a design fits the client’s goals and what trade-offs it creates.

examFormat.heading: Account Engagement Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. It uses multiple-choice questions about Account Engagement consulting work.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Many questions describe a B2B marketing goal and ask how to design the related scoring, nurture, Salesforce sync, or reporting approach.
bestWayToPass: Connect scoring and grading to sales criteria: Use engagement to measure interest and profile details to measure fit. Agree with sales on what makes a prospect ready.
Plan nurture programs: Map the prospect’s goal, entry conditions, decision points, and exit conditions before building branches and waits.
Plan Salesforce sync: Check the connector user’s access, choose which system controls each shared field, and learn how to investigate sync errors.
Make campaign reporting useful: Understand which campaign and opportunity measures answer the client’s questions about pipeline and revenue.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers strategic B2B marketing automation design with Account Engagement (Pardot), including lead scoring models, Engagement Studio nurture programs, Salesforce sync architecture, and campaign attribution.

keyConcepts.h2: Account Engagement Consultant: Key Exam Concepts

blocks.heading: Plan the implementation
blocks.body: Start with the client’s marketing goals, teams, Salesforce setup, and data. Then decide how Account Engagement business units, user access, connector settings, and campaigns should be organized. Match the design to the client’s structure instead of adding complexity without a need.

blocks.heading: Choose the right automation
blocks.body: Engagement Studio is for nurturing prospects through a planned series of steps. Automation Rules evaluate criteria and can take ongoing actions. Segmentation Rules create a list based on criteria at a point in time. Choose the tool that fits the job and the timing the client needs.

blocks.heading: Align marketing and sales campaigns
blocks.body: Account Engagement campaigns commonly show a prospect’s first marketing touch. Salesforce campaigns and campaign influence support broader campaign tracking and opportunity reporting. Plan campaign hierarchy and member statuses so the teams can interpret the results consistently.

blocks.heading: Design scoring, grading, and segments
blocks.body: Scoring reflects a prospect’s activity, such as visits and email engagement. Grading reflects how well the prospect matches the client’s target profile. Scoring categories can separate interest in different products. Segmentation Rules create a list at a point in time, while Dynamic Lists keep matching records up to date.

blocks.heading: Report on business results
blocks.body: Choose reports that answer the client’s questions. Teams may need to see prospect activity, campaign performance, or how marketing relates to pipeline and revenue. Agree on the measures and data definitions before building dashboards.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The consultant exam focuses on designing Account Engagement around a client’s marketing and sales process. Start with the business goal, then choose the configuration and automation that support it.

blocks.heading: Scoring and grading
blocks.body: Scoring estimates interest from activity; grading estimates fit with the client’s target profile. Agree on useful thresholds with sales before automating handoff.

blocks.heading: Nurture programs
blocks.body: Plan the prospect’s journey first. Set clear entry and exit conditions, then choose where behavior or CRM data should change the path.

blocks.heading: Salesforce sync
blocks.body: Check which Salesforce user connects the systems and what access that user needs. For each shared field, know which system should control updates.

blocks.heading: Forms and tracking
blocks.body: Choose a native form when the client can use Account Engagement’s page components. Use a form handler when an existing external form must remain in place. Configure tracking with the client’s domains and privacy requirements in mind.

blocks.heading: Campaign reporting
blocks.body: Set up campaign structure and member statuses so marketing and sales use the same definitions. Use measures tied to pipeline or revenue when reporting business value.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales team ignores prospect scores because many high-scoring prospects are poor fits. What should the consultant review first?
options: Check whether the scoring model matches sales qualification
Whether sales users have completed a product navigation course
Whether the client needs more nurture-program licenses
How often the connector checks for new prospect activity
sampleQuestions.explanation: The scoring and grading design should reflect the signals sales uses to qualify prospects.
whyWrong: Training on navigation does not fix scores that fail to identify useful prospects.
The issue is whether the qualification model is useful, not the number of licenses.
A sync schedule does not make the scoring criteria more relevant.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants its grading profile to identify prospects who resemble its best customers. What should shape the profile?
options: The client’s expected number of new prospects per month
The order in which the client opened its sales regions
The traits shared by its strongest existing customers
The number of questions on its lead capture form
sampleQuestions.explanation: Grading measures fit, so use attributes that describe the client’s target customers.
whyWrong: Monthly prospect volume does not describe who is a good fit.
Region launch dates do not define the target profile.
The form’s field count does not determine which traits matter.

sampleQuestions.question: Marketing wants qualified prospects assigned to sales once they meet agreed score and grade thresholds. What should the consultant use?
options: A weekly meeting where staff select prospects by hand
Automation rule using score and grade thresholds
A static segmentation list that is rebuilt each morning
A completion action added to every form in the account
sampleQuestions.explanation: An automation rule can keep evaluating prospects and assign those who meet the agreed criteria.
whyWrong: Manual review adds delay and does not automate the handoff.
A static list is a point-in-time group, not ongoing threshold evaluation.
A form completion action runs on a form event, not when a prospect later qualifies.

sampleQuestions.question: A client plans to sync many fields that marketing and sales do not use. What concern should the consultant raise?
options: The connector will automatically turn off after a field limit is reached
Unneeded data can add noise in Salesforce and create extra sync work
Account Engagement will stop calculating prospect scores
Salesforce will reject every record with marketing fields
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sync only useful fields to keep CRM records clear and limit unnecessary sync activity.
whyWrong: A field count does not by itself mean the connector will turn off.
Field sync does not stop the scoring feature.
Salesforce can store custom fields; the concern is whether the data is useful.

sampleQuestions.question: A company has three brands with separate audiences and marketing teams. What should the consultant evaluate?
options: Giving each brand a separate Salesforce org by default
Whether enough custom fields exist for each brand
Use business units to separate brand teams and prospect data
Sharing one tracking domain across every brand
sampleQuestions.explanation: Business units can separate marketing assets, prospects, and access when the organization needs that structure.
whyWrong: Separate Salesforce orgs are not automatically required for separate brands.
Custom-field count does not answer how to organize brands and access.
A shared tracking domain may not suit every brand’s needs.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants to learn more about returning prospects without making the first form longer. What should the consultant recommend?
options: Requiring every profile field on the first visit
Progressive profiling on later visits
Removing the consent language from the form
Turning off scoring for people who submit the form
sampleQuestions.explanation: Progressive profiling asks for a few new details on later visits, keeping the first form shorter.
whyWrong: Requiring every field at once can make the first form longer.
Progressive profiling does not remove consent requirements.
Scoring is separate from how a form gathers profile details.

sampleQuestions.question: Prospects are being assigned to sales users who have left the company. What should the consultant inspect?
options: The score needed before a prospect can be assigned
The tracking domain used on the company’s landing pages
Review assignment rules and the users they assign prospects to
How often the connector syncs records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Assignment rules may still point to inactive users or outdated queues.
whyWrong: The threshold does not explain why assignments go to former employees.
Tracking domains do not choose the assignment owner.
Sync timing is separate from the owner selected by assignment rules.

sampleQuestions.question: Before building a nurture program, what should the consultant clarify with the client?
options: The planned email volume for each calendar month
The total size of the prospect database
The approved colors for email templates
The next decision the program should help prospects reach
sampleQuestions.explanation: The program should support a clear prospect goal; that goal guides the messages and branches.
whyWrong: Email volume alone does not explain what the program should achieve.
Database size does not define the journey or decision.
Brand colors do not determine the nurture path.

sampleQuestions.question: A new nurture program causes a sharp rise in unsubscribes. What should the consultant investigate first?
options: Emails sent too often or without relevant content
Whether the tracking domain is verified for email sending
Whether the program includes a wait step between every email
Whether prospects had a grade before entering the program
sampleQuestions.explanation: Too many messages or irrelevant content can lead prospects to unsubscribe.
whyWrong: A tracking domain can matter for tracking, but it does not explain message relevance or frequency.
Wait steps alone do not ensure that the program suits its audience.
Having a grade is not required for every nurture program.

sampleQuestions.question: A marketer needs to keep certain prospects out of one email send. What is a suppression list for?
options: To store prospects who have not yet been assigned to sales
To collect the highest-scoring prospects for a special send
To exclude selected prospects from that send
To track which prospects opened an earlier email
sampleQuestions.explanation: A suppression list excludes its members from an email send.
whyWrong: Assignment status is a separate prospect attribute.
A suppression list does not select recipients for priority.
Opens are tracked as email activity, not by a suppression list.

sampleQuestions.question: A client has an external web form whose design and markup cannot change. Which Account Engagement option fits?
options: Use a form handler with the existing external form
A native form that replaces the external form
A segmentation rule that collects the submitted fields
A completion action added to the existing web page
sampleQuestions.explanation: A form handler can receive submissions while the client keeps the external form markup.
whyWrong: A native form would replace the form the client needs to keep.
A segmentation rule groups records; it does not accept form submissions.
A completion action runs after an Account Engagement action and does not receive the external form data by itself.

sampleQuestions.question: Why configure an Account Engagement tracking domain with the client’s own domain?
options: It sets the number of landing pages the account can publish
It is required to record any prospect activity at all
It removes the need to follow consent rules
Use a tracking domain branded for the client
sampleQuestions.explanation: A branded tracking domain lets tracked links and pages use the client’s domain.
whyWrong: The domain does not set the landing-page limit.
Tracking can work with other configured domains as well.
A branded domain does not replace consent obligations.

sampleQuestions.question: A client has many inactive prospects and wants to protect email deliverability. What is a sensible plan?
options: Send the same large campaign to all prospects to find active people
Increase send frequency across the full database
Delete all prospects who have not engaged recently
Re-engage inactive prospects, then suppress nonresponders
sampleQuestions.explanation: Give inactive prospects a clear chance to re-engage, then reduce sends to those who do not respond.
whyWrong: A large blast to everyone may harm deliverability.
More frequent messages can worsen engagement and deliverability.
Immediate deletion may discard records before the client confirms its retention needs.

sampleQuestions.question: A client’s board asks whether marketing automation contributes to business results. Which measures best answer the question?
options: How many emails and landing pages the team created
Pipeline and revenue linked to marketing
How much the prospect database grew
How many automation rules and programs are active
sampleQuestions.explanation: Pipeline and revenue measures connect marketing activity to business outcomes.
whyWrong: Content volume measures output, not its business result.
Database growth does not show whether marketing influenced sales.
The number of automations does not show the value they create.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the consultant’s main responsibility during an Account Engagement implementation?
options: Design how the platform supports the client’s process
Write every email and landing page the client will publish
Manage the client’s sending reputation after launch
Build every automation rule requested without review
sampleQuestions.explanation: The consultant learns how the client works and designs how Account Engagement will support that process.
whyWrong: The consultant’s role is solution design, not necessarily writing every piece of campaign content.
Ongoing deliverability operations are not the main implementation role.
The consultant should assess requests against requirements rather than implement them without review.
